problem: Prior map-based navigation (FloNa, HAM-Nav, etc.) keeps floor-plan/sketch interpretation coupled to a dedicated execution policy, so pretrained VLN executors cannot be reused. Directly prompting a VLM with a map and start-goal markers omits turns and gets turn directions wrong.
motivation: Non-experts can naturally give a human-readable map and a marked destination, but robots act from egocentric observations. Compiling map-level intent into the language input of pretrained VLN policies would let executors be swapped without retraining the map-to-language modules. Spatial route reasoning by VLMs on schematic maps is unreliable, so an explicit route scaffold is needed before verbalization.
key_idea: Generate an explicit route scaffold on the map with start-goal-line conditional flow matching (deforming the straight start-goal line into a map-conditioned route), overlay it for a frozen VLM to write an instruction, and feed that instruction to a frozen pretrained VLN policy.
insight: Separating route inference from verbalization helps: Raw direct generation reaches SR 24.2 versus 54.5 for SGL-CFM on floor plans. A scaffold alone is not enough: Gaussian-source CFM (SR 24.2) is no better than Raw, and A* (SR 30.3) has similar nFD to SGL-CFM but much lower RIA/OIA, so preserving salient turn structure matters more than geometric closeness. Per-difficulty audit shows hard routes have high upstream correctness (100% route, 88.9% instruction) but only 11.1% SR, so the remaining loss is in executor execution.
method: Ordered route representation: each route is K=48 waypoints in normalized map coordinates via uniform arc-length resampling, with endpoints fixed to start and goal.
Map conditioning: the RGB map plus Gaussian start and goal heatmaps form a 5x256x256 input, encoded by an ImageNet-initialized ResNet-18 into 256 spatial tokens (d=128).
SGL-CFM: the source is the deterministic straight line X0=Line(s,g) rather than Gaussian noise. A linear-interpolation flow-matching loss trains a velocity field toward the GT route X1.

Velocity network: a temporal 1-D U-Net with multi-level cross-attention (encoder, bottleneck, decoder) to the map tokens. Inference integrates from the line with 100 Heun steps, with endpoints pinned.

Route-guided instruction compilation: the scaffold is drawn as a polyline overlay with start/goal markers, and a frozen VLM (Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview) is prompted to write short imperative instructions with explicit left/right turns, landmarks and a destination statement.

Executor-decoupled execution: a frozen VLN policy (JanusVLN by default; NaVILA and OmniNav tested) gets only the instruction and egocentric views through observation/action adapters, never the map or scaffold.

RouteScribe Metric Suite: RIA (generated route vs GT route), OIA (instruction vs overlay) and GIA (instruction vs GT) compare major-turn sequences and destination. Also GoalAcc, nFD and a blinded expert audit.

setting.backbone: Route generator: ResNet-18 + temporal 1-D U-Net flow matching (trained); Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (frozen) for instructions; JanusVLN (frozen) as default VLN executor
setting.training_data: Route generator only: 1,676 human-annotated routes from 60 floor plans; fine-tuned on 160 routes from 15 sketch maps for sketch adaptation. VLM and VLN are frozen with no training.
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB from three elevated RGB-D cameras (executor-specific formats); the map is used only upstream
setting.action_space: Executor-native VLN actions converted to robot commands by a deterministic adapter
setting.privileged: Known start location and initial heading aligned with the departure direction; LiDAR used only for trajectory evaluation; user-specified start/goal on the map

numbers_note: All benchmarks are the authors' own real-robot or offline sets, not standard VLN benchmarks; splits are labeled 'test' as the closest official word. Baseline rows (Raw, A*, G-CFM) were excluded per the rules.
results: On real-robot floor-plan tests SGL-CFM reaches SR 54.5 / SPL 0.504 / NE 5.388, versus A* (SR 30.3, SPL 0.277), Gaussian CFM (24.2, 0.210) and Raw (24.2, 0.214). On the sketch map SR is 36.4 versus 9.1 for all three baselines. Different VLMs and VLN executors can be swapped in without upstream retraining, but executor quality strongly affects success (JanusVLN SR 50.0 vs NaVILA 22.7 and OmniNav 9.1).
limitations: Small real-world evaluation (33 floor-plan and 11 sketch specs) in office environments, with a fixed K=48 and 256x256 map input; larger or longer routes may need hierarchical representations.
Assumes a known start location and an initial heading aligned with the departure direction.
Multi-turn routes lose most success at the executor (hard routes SR 11.1% despite high upstream correctness), so overall performance depends on the VLN policy.
